title: A Centenary of Justice -- Ch. 9: A Benchbook for Judicial Excellence

stances.claim: Judicial excellence requires not only the right people but the right tools and environment: the Benchbook -- 'the judicial bible' -- is a necessary component of judicial reform because it gives judges instant, reliable information to rule 'on the spot' during trial and thus the 'strength and confidence' to dispense quality justice speedily. Reforming the judiciary means equipping it, not merely exhorting it.

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 9 of 'A Centenary of Justice' reproduces CJP's short Closing Remarks at the launch of the Benchbook on January 20, 2001 at the new SC Centenary Building. After restating the centenary's goals and theme ('Katarungan at Bayan, Magpakailanman'), he frames the Judicial Reform Program as one that uplifts judges, their tools and their working environment, and enhances the four 'Ins' of a great magistrate -- integrity, intelligence, independence and industry (an early articulation of his signature formula). The Benchbook, which CJ Davide calls 'the judicial bible,' is presented as a necessary component of that program: a single, handy volume -- issued in print, CD ROM, disc or webpage form -- that lets judges resolve issues 'on the spot' during trial, assuring 'up-to-date, reliable and dependable information' and giving them 'strength and confidence' in their rulings. He ties it to the constitutional command that decisions explain the facts and law 'correctly, clearly, completely, and concisely' (the 4 Cs), calling the Benchbook 'an indispensable guide for the speedy dispensation of quality justice.' He closes by thanking the producers and donors -- the Australian government (Ambassador John Buckley), Australian AID, the Philippines-Australia Governance Facility, the International Development Law Institute, the Philippine Judicial Academy, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank, along with the authors, editors, consultants, advisers and the SC's Project Management Office -- and, in Filipino, appeals for continued help in advancing 'Katarungan at Bayan, Magpakailanman.'
